sections.h2: Where the county keeps deeds and liens
sections.html:
Look to the Brazoria County Clerk's Recording Department, located at 237 East Locust, Suite 102, Angleton, TX 77515, in the Administration Building. The recording and vitals line is 979-864-1059. Trustee sale notices go up at the courthouse in Angleton, the county seat.

The clerk's website hosts a searchable real property database. Use it at home or on the public computers in the Angleton office. New users create a login and answer a verification email before searching. Clerks are recorders rather than qualified examiners, so a title search is not something they do for you. Keep in mind that the website is not the official repository, and state law requires some details to be redacted.

  • Plain copies: $1.00 per page
  • Certified copies: $1.00 per page plus $5.00 per document, mailed by regular post only
  • Copy requests go through an online application, and payment follows an approval email

One page of deed costs $25.00 to record: $10.00 for records management, $10.00 for the records archive and $5.00 for the first page. Every additional page adds $4.00. Names indexed beyond the first five add $0.25 each.

Sloppy filing costs extra. A deed with no grantee mailing address owes the greater of $25 or twice the filing fee on top of normal charges. The fee for a page doubles if names are not typed or printed under each signature, and doubles again for a page lacking a heading that identifies the document type.

A long checklist comes from the clerk, and missing one line can get a deed rejected. Since January 1, 2026, anyone presenting a real property document in person must show photo ID to the clerk, under Local Government Code 191.010.

  • Original signatures, with each signer's name printed or typed beneath, and a notary acknowledgment with a clear, dark seal
  • English language, or a certified translation attached
  • White paper between 8.5 x 11 and 8.5 x 14 inches, with type of at least 8 point in black or blue ink
  • A 3 inch top margin on page one and a heading naming the document type
  • A legal description showing the property lies in Brazoria County, or a reference to a prior recording that does
  • The Notice of Confidentiality Rights in 12 point bold type or 12 point capitals on any transfer to or from an individual

The county page also explains Senate Bill 30, effective September 1, 2021, which gives an owner a court process to have discriminatory restrictions in old records reviewed, with no filing fee under the statute.

E-recording is open only to filers qualified under Local Government Code 195.003, through Simplifile, CSC/Ingeo, Nationwide Title Clearing, ePN, Indecomm or hopdox. Re-recording an e-recorded deed requires a certified copy or the original with the first and last pages of the e-recorded version attached.

The fee page also prices several mail and data services. Expedited service is $5.00 plus the mail option you choose, which is $5.00 for 3 day priority post or $30.00 for FedEx overnight. Title plants that want bulk data can buy daily, weekly or two week CDs of images and indices at $6.00, $8.00 and $12.00, or daily and weekly FTP at $3.00 and $5.00.

Each faxed page is $1.00, with a usage charge of $1.00 inside the calling area or $2.00 outside it. Vital records cannot be faxed. Copies of 11 x 17 pages are $2.00 each, and a 24 x 36 plat or map copy is $5.00 a page.

This Gulf Coast county faces flood and hurricane exposure, which affects how land is held and insured. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 419,080 people, a 12.6 percent gain over April 2020, living in 162,298 housing units, of which 74.1 percent are owner occupied. The median value of owner occupied homes is $301,600 and median gross rent is $1,454. Pearland is the largest city, and the Brazosport area includes Lake Jackson, Clute, Freeport and Surfside Beach.

sections.h2: The appraisal district and the tax office
sections.html:
Values and exemptions are handled by the Brazoria Central Appraisal District, 500 North Chenango in Angleton. The clerk only records the deed. Appraisal notices are due by April 1 for single-family homes and by May 1 for other property, or soon after.

Under Senate Bill 1801 the district audits homestead exemptions, reviewing each residence homestead at least once every five tax years. An owner who receives no letter does not need to file again. The Tax Assessor-Collector's office, at 111 E. Locust in Angleton, takes calls about tax bills at 979-864-1320.

State rules set the school district homestead exemption at $140,000, with $60,000 more for owners who are 65 or older or disabled. A tax lien attaches every January 1, and taxes unpaid after January 31 carry penalty and interest. When a house is sold, the recorded deed is what moves ownership on the appraisal rolls, so file it promptly after closing.

sections.h2: Recording problems that slow a sale
sections.html:
Three problems come up again and again: missing notary details, a legal description that differs from the prior deed, and unreleased liens. A release of a paid-off lien is itself a recordable instrument, so ask the lender for it in writing and confirm it appears in the clerk's index.

An inherited house needs more proof. Filing an affidavit of heirship with the county clerk records a sworn statement that no court has verified, and nothing requires a buyer or lender to accept it. An order from the probate court, or a transfer on death deed recorded before the owner's death, gives a buyer firmer footing.

Foreclosure timing also shows up in these records. A notice of sale must be posted at the courthouse and filed with the clerk at least 21 days before the first-Tuesday auction, and Brazoria County charges $8.00 for a trustee notice.

The Brazoria clerk's index is the place to confirm a release was filed after a payoff, so check it yourself rather than assuming the lender recorded one. Print the recorded release and keep it with your sale papers.

A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork, but the title company still needs a clean record. Allow a few days before closing to catch missing releases.

faqs.q: What is the first-page recording fee?
faqs.a: The charge is $25.00. Records management and the records archive are $10.00 each, and the first page adds $5.00. Later pages are $4.00 apiece.

faqs.q: Do I need photo ID to record a deed?
faqs.a: Yes, when you file in person. Anyone handing over a real property document has had to show photo ID since January 1, 2026, a rule in Local Government Code 191.010.

faqs.q: Can clerk staff search the records for me?
faqs.a: No. The clerks are recorders and are not qualified examiners, so you search the online database yourself or use the public computers at 237 East Locust in Angleton.

faqs.q: How do I get a certified copy of a deed?
faqs.a: Search the database for the document number and page count, then submit the online copy application. Certified copies cost $1.00 per page plus $5.00 per document and are sent by regular mail.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed has no grantee mailing address?
faqs.a: The clerk adds a penalty fee. Texas Property Code 11.003 sets it at the greater of $25 or twice the statutory filing fee, charged on top of the regular recording cost.
